Genesis 1

Genesis narrative prose. English is rendered from the Hebrew; select a word or verse number to study it. English is rendered from the Hebrew. Tap a verse number for the original Hebrew, earlier versions and resource evidence.

Beside elohim: SG singular agreement, PL plural agreement, ? checked, undetermined.

In the beginning, elohim created the skies and the earth. And the earth was unformed and empty, and darkness lay over the surface of the deep, and ruach elohim was hovering over the surface of the water. Then elohim said, “Let there be light.” And there was light. And elohim saw the light, that it was good. And elohim made a separation between the light and the darkness. And elohim gave the name “day” to the light, and to the darkness he gave the name “night.” And there was evening, and there was morning: one day. And elohim said, “Let there be an expanse in the middle of the waters, and let it be separating water from water.” And elohim made the expanse and separated the waters that were below the expanse from the waters that were above the expanse. And it was so. And elohim called the expanse sky. And there was evening, and there was morning: a second day. And elohim said, “Let the waters under the sky be gathered to one place, and let the dry land appear.” And it was so. And elohim called the dry land earth, and he called the gathering of the waters seas. And elohim saw that it was good. Then elohim said, “Let the earth sprout vegetation: plants producing seed, fruit trees bearing fruit according to their kind, with their seed in them, on the earth.” And it was so. And the earth brought forth vegetation: plants producing seed, according to their kind, and trees bearing fruit whose seed is in it, according to their kind. And elohim saw that it was good. And there was evening, and there was morning: day three. Then elohim said, “Let there be lights in the expanse of the heavens to separate between the day and the night. And let them serve for signs, and for appointed times, and for days and years.” “And let them be lights in the expanse of the heavens to give light on the earth.” And it was so. And elohim made the two great lights: the larger light for rule over the day, and the smaller light for rule over the night, and the stars. And elohim placed them in the expanse of the heavens to give light on the earth. and to rule over the day and over the night, and to distinguish between the light and the darkness. And elohim saw that it was good. And there was evening, and there was morning: a fourth day. And elohim said, “Let the waters swarm with swarms of living creatures, and let birds fly above the earth, across the face of the expanse of the heavens.” And elohim created the great sea creatures and every living creature that moves, with which the waters swarmed, according to their kind, and every winged bird according to their kind. And elohim saw that it was good. And elohim yvarekh them, saying, “Reproduce and increase and fill the waters in the seas, and let the birds increase on the earth.” And there was evening, and there was morning: a fifth day. And elohim said, “Let the earth bring out living creatures according to their kind: livestock, and crawling creatures, and wild animals of the earth according to their kind.” And it was so. And elohim made the wild animals of the earth according to their kind, and the livestock according to their kind, and every creeping creature of the ground according to their kind. And elohim saw that it was good. Then elohim said, “Let us make humankind in our image, according to our likeness, and let them rule over the fish of the sea, and over the birds of the sky, and over the livestock, and over all the earth, and over every crawling creature that crawls on the earth.” And elohim created the human in his image; in the image of elohim he created him; male and female he created them. And elohim yvarekh them, and elohim said to them, “Have offspring and increase in number, and fill the earth and subdue it, and rule over the fish of the sea, and over the birds of the sky, and over every living creature that moves on the earth.” And elohim said, “Look, I have given to you every plant producing seed that is on the surface of all the earth, and every tree in which there is fruit of a tree producing seed. It will be for you for food.” “And for every animal of the earth, and for every bird of the sky, and for everything that crawls on the earth, that has in it living breath, all green plants are for food.” And it was so. And elohim saw everything that he had made, and look, it was very good. And there was evening, and there was morning: the sixth day.

# John 21 source attribution

SBL Greek New Testament, edited by Michael W. Holmes; copyright 2010 Society of Biblical Literature and Logos Bible Software. Supplied Faithlife/SBLGNT text and current LICENSE: [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/), without warranties. Source: https://github.com/Faithlife/SBLGNT. John 21 extracted, tokenized and NFC normalized; raw token spelling retained. See data/raw/SBLGNT-About.md and SBLGNT-LICENSE.txt for supplied notices.

Tauber, J. K., ed. (2017), *MorphGNT: SBLGNT Edition*, version 6.12, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.376200. https://github.com/morphgnt/sblgnt. Morphological parsing, normalization and lemmatization: [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/). The supplied README links an older SBLGNT EULA for its text; we import surface text independently from Faithlife's supplied current CC BY 4.0 text. John 21 analysis extracted and aligned. The combined master and adapted analysis are distributed under CC BY-SA 3.0, retaining the independent CC BY 4.0 source notices. Derived SQLite contains the same adapted data and carries the same notices. No claim that MorphGNT itself has relicensed its text.

STEPBible.org, Tyndale House Cambridge, Translators Amalgamated Greek New Testament (TAGNT): https://github.com/STEPBible/STEPBible-Data, [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). John 21 lexical identifiers, dictionary glosses, morphology, edition support and structured variant fields extracted. Running English/Spanish, sub-meanings and explanatory notes excluded. Sanitization and alignment are modifications; no source text corrections asserted. Upstream requests referring readers to its repository for current data. Edition codes are edition support, not dated manuscript witnesses.

Exact upstream commits and local evidence files are recorded in data/sources.tsv. Supplied downloads were fetched 2026-10-20; this implementation performed no network access. Local license evidence is checked again by the import script. data/raw/manifest.tsv records SHA-256 hashes of supplied inputs. No endorsement by the source creators is implied.

STEPBible.org, Tyndale House Cambridge, Translators Amalgamated Hebrew OT (TAHOT), https://github.com/STEPBible/STEPBible-Data (commit ed476a8ee6e3f7b3a46fc48af6c7dabc02387b1d), [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). ## Genesis 1 (Hebrew numbering; LXX Psalm 80)
`data/psa81.jsonl` adapts the pinned STEPBible TAHOT by STEPBible.org / Tyndale House Cambridge, CC BY 4.0, commit ed476a8ee6e3f7b3a46fc48af6c7dabc02387b1d. Source and license: https://github.com/STEPBible/STEPBible-Data and `data/raw/TAHOT/TAHOT-Job-Sng.txt` header. Changes: select Genesis 1, split Hebrew marks into fields, remove slash segmentation for display, retain segmentation in surface_raw, strip all English glosses and notes, use explicit Hebrew references. Morphology and transliteration remain TAHOT's. No separate OSHB/WLC source was imported.

`data/resources/PSA.81.jsonl` and the reader reproduce Swete Psalm 80 word forms from Nathan Smith's nathans/lxx-swete / Open Greek and Latin First1KGreek, pinned 26bad3eb42bba98471d154c954e36a6f30a0279d; data CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://github.com/nathans/lxx-swete). Adaptation: group forms by verse and attach Hebrew verse co-occurrence metadata. The derived Greek-form layer is CC BY-SA 4.0; attribution and ShareAlike must accompany redistribution. Hebrew TAHOT fields retain CC BY 4.0. These forms are secondary cross-reference evidence, never the Hebrew render base.

OpenBible.info cross-reference data, CC BY 4.0 (https://www.openbible.info/labs/cross-references/), is filtered by Hebrew lexical overlap and always flagged BORDERLINE. See `data/sources.tsv` and the raw manifest for pins. Resource and detector candidates are project-generated adaptations, not semantic conclusions.

OSHB morphhb Psalms: Open Scriptures Hebrew Bible contributors, [morphhb](https://github.com/openscriptures/morphhb), commit 3d15126fb1ef74867fc1434be1942e837932691f. Morphology and segmentation CC BY 4.0 (data/raw/OSHB/LICENSE.md); based on public-domain Westminster Leningrad Codex. Morpheme data is an adaptation aligned to TAHOT; source-specific vocalization is preserved.
